In the second of these, the Section of Answers, is the analysis of the root condition (hetupaccaya): "A wholesome state [is related] to a wholesome state by way of the root condition..."
Condition: Wholesome roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A wholesome state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state. Wholesome roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for mind-produced matter.
A wholesome state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for both wholesome and indeterminate states.

“Wholesome roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter,” thus it was taught by the Blessed One after analyzing it in detail in such passages.
… “A wholesome state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state; wholesome roots [are a condition] for associated [states].”

[It is] a condition for the aggregates by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). A wholesome state (*kusala-dhamma*) is a condition for an indeterminate state (*abyākata-dhamma*) by way of the root-condition:
wholesome roots are a condition for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) by way of the root-condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate states by way of the root-condition: wholesome roots [are a condition] for their associated [states].
“The aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.
Analysis of the Object-Condition.
Question: “By that, friend... [etc. ...by the Fully Enlightened One in the seventh of the seven treatises in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka...”
In the *Paṭṭhāna-mahāpakaraṇa*, among the twenty-four *paṭṭhānas*, in the first, the *Dhammānuloma-paṭṭhāna*; among the twenty-two triplets (*tīka*), in the first, the *Kusala-ttika*;
among the seven great sections (*mahāvāra*), in the seventh, the *Pañhāvāra*; among the four methods (*naya*), in the first, the *Paccayānuloma-naya*;
and within the three sections known as the *Pucchāvāra*, *Vissajjanāvāra*, and *Saṅkhyāvāra*, in the second, the *Vissajjanāvāra*.

How is the second analysis, the Analysis of the Object Condition (*Ārammaṇa-paccaya-vibhaṅga*), taught in detail among the twenty-four analyses beginning with the Analysis of the Root Condition (*Hetu-paccaya-vibhaṅga*)?
The answer: Venerable Sir, it is in the seventh treatise among the seven books of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, namely, the *Anantanaya-samanta-paṭṭhāna*.
In the *Mahāpakaraṇa*, within the twenty-four *paṭṭhānas*, in the first, the *Dhammānuloma-paṭṭhāna*; within the twenty-two *tikas*, in the first, the *Kusala-tika*;
within the seven *mahāvāras*, in the seventh, the *Pañhāvāra*; within the four *nayās*, in the first, the *Paccayānuloma-naya*;
and within the three *vāras*, in the second, the *Vibhaṅgavāra*—in the twenty-four [sections] beginning with the *Hetupaccaya-vibhaṅga*.
In the *Vibhaṅgas*, the second section is the Analysis of the Object Condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya-vibhaṅga*): "A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the object condition.
Having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, and having performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews it; one reviews former well-performed deeds;
having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna; the trainees (*sekkhā*) [review] change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*)."
They review it; they review purification. Learners, having emerged from the path, review the path.

Learners or worldlings (puthujjana) practice insight into the wholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. They know the mind of one possessing a wholesome mind by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds.
Wholesome [consciousness] of the base of infinite space [is related] to wholesome [consciousness] of the base of infinite consciousness.

“...is a condition by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya). Wholesome consciousness of the base of nothingness is a condition by way of object-condition for wholesome consciousness of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Wholesome aggregates are a condition by way of object-condition for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma, and the knowledge of future existences,” and so forth, was said by the Blessed One.

It has been taught by analyzing it in detail. Question: In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, friends, among the seven treatises, in the seventh, the Great Treatise on the *Paṭṭhāna*, there are twenty-four... [conditions]. Regarding the analysis of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya-vibhaṅga*). Question: ...in the seventh, the Great Treatise on the *Paṭṭhāna*, among the twenty-four... [great divisions]. Regarding the analysis of the predominance condition. Question: ...in the seventh, the Great Treatise on the *Paṭṭhāna*, among the twenty-four... [great divisions], how many conditions are there? Answer: There are twenty-one conditions. Which twenty-one? They are: root condition, object condition, predominance condition, proximity condition, contiguity condition, conascence condition, mutuality condition, dependence condition, strong-dependence condition, prenascence condition, postnascence condition, repetition condition, kamma condition, resultant condition, nutriment condition, faculty condition, jhāna condition, path condition, association condition, dissociation condition, presence condition, absence condition, and non-disappearance condition. These are the twenty-one conditions. What is the predominance condition? There are four kinds of predominance: predominance as object, predominance as conascence, predominance as support, and predominance as decisive support. What is predominance as object? It is the state of being a predominant factor for a consciousness and its mental concomitants by way of being an object. What is predominance as conascence? It is the state of being a predominant factor for conascent states by way of being a conascent predominant factor.

What is predominance as support? It is the state of being a predominant factor for derived matter by way of being a support-predominant factor. What is predominance as decisive support? It is the state of being a predominant factor for a consciousness and its mental concomitants by way of being a decisive support-predominant factor. This is called the predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal predominance condition and external predominance condition. What is the internal predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own states by way of being an internal predominant factor. What is the external predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for another’s states by way of being an external predominant factor. This is called the external predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal-external predominance condition and external-internal predominance condition. What is the internal-external predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own and another’s states by way of being an internal-external predominant factor. What is the external-internal predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for another’s and one’s own states by way of being an external-internal predominant factor. This is called the external-internal predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal-internal predominance condition and external-external predominance condition. What is the internal-internal predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own states by way of being an internal-internal predominant factor. What is the external-external predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for another’s states by way of being an external-external predominant factor. This is called the external-external predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal-predominance condition and external-predominance condition. What is the internal-predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own states by way of being an internal-predominant factor. What is the external-predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for another’s states by way of being an external-predominant factor. This is called the external-predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal-external-predominance condition and external-internal-predominance condition. What is the internal-external-predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own and another’s states by way of being an internal-external-predominant factor. What is the external-internal-predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for another’s and one’s own states by way of being an external-internal-predominant factor. This is called the external-internal-predominance condition. Furthermore, the predominance condition is of two kinds: internal-internal-predominance condition and external-external-predominance condition. What is the internal-internal-predominance condition? It is the state of being a predominant factor for one’s own states by way of being an internal-internal-predominant factor. What is the external-external-predominance condition? In the *Paṭṭhāna*, within the first section on the "Conformity of Dhammas" (*dhammānulomika-paṭṭhāna*), among the twenty-two triplets (*tika*), in the first— the "Wholesome Triplet" (*kusalattika*)— within the seven great sections (*mahāvāra*),

in the seventh— the "Question Section" (*pañhāvāra*)— among the four methods (*naya*), in the first— the "Method of Positive Conditions" (*paccayānuloma-naya*)— within the three sections reckoned as questions and answers, in the second—
the "Analysis Section" (*vibhaṅgavāra*) reckoned as the answers— among the twenty-four [divisions] beginning with the analysis of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya-vibhaṅga*).
How is the third analysis, the Analysis of the Dominant Condition (*adhipatipaccaya*), taught in detail within the *Vibhaṅgas*?

The answer: Venerable sir, among the twenty-four bases (*paṭṭhāna*) in the seventh treatise, the Great Treatise (*Mahāpakaraṇa*), of the *Anantanayasamantapaṭṭhāna* within the seven treatises of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, it is taught in detail in the first base, the Base Concordant with Phenomena (*dhammānulomika-paṭṭhāna*), in twenty-two...

In the first *tikas* (triads), within the first triad of the wholesome (*kusala*), among the seven great sections, in the seventh section on questions, among the four methods (*naya*), in the first method—the method of positive conditional relations (*paccayānuloma*)—there are three sections known as the "questions" and the "answers.

In the second of these, the section on analysis (*vibhaṅga*) consisting of the answers, among the twenty-four analyses beginning with the analysis of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*), this is the third: the analysis of the predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

“A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). [It is] object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and conascence-predominance (*sahajātādhipati*). Regarding object-predominance:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), one esteems and reviews that;
or one esteems and reviews former well-performed deeds; or, having emerged from a meditative absorption (*jhāna*), one [esteems and reviews] the absorption.”
One esteems and reviews it; trainees esteem and review change-of-lineage; they esteem and review purification;
trainees, having emerged from the path, esteem and review the path.
Co-nascent predominance—wholesome predominance—is a condition by way of predominance-condition for its associated aggregates.
Thus, having analyzed it in detail, it was taught by the Blessed One through such passages as these.
Question on the Analysis of the Immediate Condition:
Venerable friend, how was the fourth analysis of the immediate condition (*anantarapaccaya*) taught in detail by the Blessed One...?
The Exposition: In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, Bhante... [etc. ...the fourth analysis of the proximity condition:
"A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the proximity condition.
Preceding wholesome aggregates are a condition for succeeding wholesome aggregates by way of the proximity condition. The adaptation..."
"Change-of-lineage is a condition for conformity; conformity is a condition for purification; change-of-lineage is a condition for the path;
purification is a condition for the path by way of proximity-condition"—thus it was taught by the Blessed One, having analyzed it in detail in such a manner.
This is the Analysis of the Co-nascent Condition (*sahajāta-paccaya-vibhaṅga*).
Question: Friend... [as above] ...how has the sixth analysis of the conascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya-vibhaṅga*) been taught in detail?
Answer: In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, Bhante... [as above] ...the sixth analysis of the conascence condition is stated as follows:
"A wholesome state (*kusala-dhamma*) is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the conascence condition; one wholesome aggregate (*khandha*) [is a condition] for three..."
The aggregates are related to the aggregates by way of co-nascence condition: three aggregates are related to one aggregate by way of co-nascence condition;
two aggregates are related to two aggregates by way of co-nascence condition. A wholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition:
wholesome aggregates are related to mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
"...condition," and so forth, it was taught by the Blessed One in detail after having analyzed it.
**Analysis of the Decisive Support Condition (Upanissaya-paccaya-vibhaṅga)** Question:
Venerable friend, how was that ninth analysis of the decisive support condition taught in detail by the Blessed One...?
The Exposition—In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, venerable sir... [as above] ...the ninth section, the Analysis of the Decisive Support Condition (*upanissaya-paccaya-vibhaṅga*):

"A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the decisive support condition. [It is] a decisive support by way of object (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), a decisive support by way of proximity (*anantarūpanissaya*), and a decisive support by way of nature (*pakatūpanissaya*).
Decisive support by way of object: having given a gift, having undertaken the precepts, and having performed the Uposatha duty..."
Making what as its support does one reflect?

… [as above] … Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): relying on faith as a decisive support, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duties, arouses jhāna, arouses insight, arouses the Path, arouses direct knowledge, and enters meditative attainment.
...arises,” and so forth; thus it was taught by the Blessed One after analyzing it in detail.

**Question on the Analysis of the Antecedent Condition:** “Friend, how was the tenth analysis of the antecedent condition (*purejāta-paccaya-vibhaṅga*) taught in detail? [The response follows: “By that [method], friend... and so forth.
The Exposition—In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, Bhante... [omitted] ...the tenth, the Analysis of the Relation of Pre-existence:
"An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the relation of pre-existence. It is object-pre-existence and base-pre-existence. Object-pre-existence:
An Arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. [He contemplates] the nose, the tongue..."
He contemplates the body, visible forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles, as well as the physical basis, through insight as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
With the divine eye he sees a visible form; with the divine ear-element he hears a sound;
the visible-form base is the object of eye-consciousness, the sound base of ear-consciousness, the odor base of nose-consciousness, and the taste base...
The sphere of tangible objects is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition. As for the pre-arising condition of the physical basis (*vatthupurejāta*):
the eye-sphere is a condition for eye-consciousness; the ear-sphere for ear-consciousness; the nose-sphere for nose-consciousness;
the tongue-sphere for tongue-consciousness; the body-sphere for body-consciousness; and the physical basis is a condition for resultant-inoperative and functional-inoperative states.
“...a condition for the aggregates by way of the pre-arising condition,” thus it was taught by the Blessed One in detail after having analyzed it.
**Analysis of the Kamma Condition** Question:
“Friend, how was the thirteenth analysis, the analysis of the kamma condition, taught in detail by the Blessed One... [as before] ...?
The Exposition—In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, Bhante... [and so forth] ...the thirteenth section, the Analysis of the Conditionality of Kamma:
"A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of kamma-condition. A wholesome volition is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of kamma-condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of kamma-condition."
Conascent and asynchronous. Conascent wholesome volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for mind-produced matter.
Asynchronous wholesome volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced matter.
A wholesome state is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for both wholesome and indeterminate states.
“Wholesome volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter,” thus it was taught by the Blessed One after analyzing it in detail,
and so forth. [This concludes] the Analysis of the Nutriment Condition.
Question: "Friend... [as above] ...how has the fifteenth analysis of the nutriment condition been taught in detail?
Answer: "In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, Bhante... [as above] ...the fifteenth analysis of the nutriment condition is as follows:
'A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the nutriment condition. Wholesome nutriments are conditions for their associated aggregates...'"

It is taught by the Blessed One in detail through such analysis as: “Conditioned by nutriment, there is a condition. A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the nutriment-condition.
Wholesome nutriments are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the nutriment-condition.
Thus it was taught.

Analysis of the Conditionality of the Faculties (Indriyapaccayavibhaṅga) Question: "Friend, how has that sixteenth analysis of the conditionality of the faculties been taught in detail by the Blessed One...?
Answer: "Venerable sir, in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka... the sixteenth analysis of the conditionality of the faculties [is taught as]: 'The wholesome...'"
“A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the faculty-condition; wholesome faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the faculty-condition.

It was taught by the Blessed One after analyzing it in detail.

The Section on Dependent Origination for the Feeling Triplet (Vedanātika Paṭiccasamuppādavāra).

Question: "Friend, after the Blessed One... [as above] ... had analyzed the first wholesome triplet in detail, how did he subsequently analyze and teach the remaining twenty-one triplets, beginning with the feeling triplet, in detail?
Answer: "In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, venerable sir... [as above] ... after analyzing the first wholesome triplet in detail..."
Immediately following that, the remaining twenty-one groups beginning with the triad of feeling are as follows:
“Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling, a state associated with pleasant feeling arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

"At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate associated with pleasant feeling, two aggregates [arise];

Dependent on one resultant aggregate, three aggregates [arise]; dependent on three aggregates...

One aggregate; two aggregates in dependence on two aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking, three aggregates in dependence on one resultant aggregate, one aggregate in dependence on three aggregates, and two aggregates in dependence on two aggregates.
Dependent on a resultant state, a state that is neither-resultant-nor-possessing-the-nature-of-result arises by way of root condition, [dependent on] the resultant [state].
"Dependent on the aggregates, mind-originated matter [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on resultant aggregates, kamma-produced matter [arises];

dependent on the aggregates, the physical bases [arise]"—in this way, the Blessed One has taught by analyzing in detail through seven great sections for each triad, and within each great section, through four methods.

Depending on a phenomenon with conflict, phenomena both with conflict and without conflict arise by way of the root condition.
Depending on one aggregate with conflict, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise; depending on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-originated matter arise.

Dependent on a non-root wholesome state, a root wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a root wholesome state, both root wholesome and non-root wholesome states arise by way of root condition.

Immediately following that is the second *dhammapaccanīyapaṭṭhāna*: “Dependent on a non-virtuous state, a non-virtuous state arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Form. Dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on a non-wholesome state, a non-wholesome state arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one resultant indeterminate or functional indeterminate aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter; dependent on three aggregates, there arises one...
The aggregates and mind-produced matter. Dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking... [etc. ...dependent on unwholesome states, a non-defined state arises by way of root condition.
